- Private (VPC-hosted / customer VPC): lead time depends on network & onboarding window; plan for 8–12 weeks for VPC provisioning + KMS integration; on-prem appliances can be longer (10–14 weeks) depending on onsite approvals.

Subject: Re: Capacity MAP & lead times for Dedicated/Private — updated timeline and acceptance criteria

Maya / Tom —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Per internal checks (Ben & Karthik), here is an updated MAP summary and firm cutoff dates to hit the 2027-06-20 pilot window:

- Key cutoff dates (to deliver reserved capacity by 2027-06-20):
  • Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved capacity): sign by 2027-05-03 latest to hit 6–8 week provisioning and routing.
  • Private (VPC deployment): sign by 2027-04-19 latest to allow 8–12 weeks for VPC onboarding, KMS/HSM integration, and security review.

- Pilot sizing (conservative | fast-ramp), model throughput approximations (measured p95 targets assume standard batching and prefix caching):
  • Llama-2-13B (quantized): conservative = 2 x H100 (~8–12 QPS sustained), fast-ramp = 4 x H100 (~16–22 QPS sustained).
  • Llama-3-70B (int8/gptq): conservative = 4 x H100 (~10–18 QPS), fast-ramp = 6 x H100 (~18–28 QPS).
  • Custom fine-tuned 13B variant: conservative = 2 x H100 (~9–14 QPS), fast-ramp = 4 x H100 (~17–24 QPS).

- Acceptance gating (minimum for pilot launch):
  1) Security: SOC2 documentation + evidence (we've attached SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf) and KMS key exchange completed.
  2) Performance: validated on 3 canonical prompt sets (latency p95 <= 300ms, success rate >= 99% under simulated QPS).
  3) Reliability: automated failover to a compatible model variant (lower-cost pool) if provisioning shortage occurs.

- KMS integration: Redwood can manage the KMS handshake for VPC deployments (we will orchestrate the exchange with your security team). For on-prem HSMs we provide a connector; Eucalyptus will need to approve firewall rules and on-prem provisioning windows.

- Contingency / hedging: if H100 inventory is constrained at provisioning time, we recommend a tranche approach: reserve an initial conservative lane (2–4 H100) with a contractual commitment to scale to the fast-ramp lane within 30 days. That reduces lead-time exposure while giving runway to validate traffic.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll update the MAP-draft-Eucalyptus-v1.xlsx with the cutoff dates and the conservative/fast-ramp lanes and send a final for signature by Fri.
- Lauren — if you can draft the PO language for a tranche-based reservation (flexible scale clause + cancellation window) and circulate, I’ll attach to the MAP.
- Ben/Karthik — please flag any additional infra caveats.

If this looks good, Tom — can you confirm the procurement slot on Mon so we can align legal and tickets?

— Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Enterprise Solutions
